body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: ffcdfa143bf779eac36d2beb2d9ef8dab8e11db0 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- One door covers every path: `collect_job` (job.rs:168) is the only caller on the generation side, reached by `GenerateOperation` (commands/operation/generate.rs:68) and by `operation::generate` (operation/generate.rs:17), which is what the MCP tool, CLI/script verbs and regenerate-all go through. I found no second entry that builds a job without it.
- Tolerance is stated and sane: 1e-9 rad, the post's identity tolerance; it is an angle from `atan2` on the rotated Z axis, not an equality test, and a non-finite rotation returns `None` (left to #327's refusal) rather than passing a NaN comparison silently.
- The refusal names the setup, the WCS slot (G54..), the tilt in degrees, and the fix (Part alignment).
- Scope is `Kind::Mill` only; yaw-only WCS still generates. 3+2 tilts are an op parameter (`tilt`), not a WCS rotation, so they do not touch this check (read, not run through every multiaxis suite).
- `lib.rs` only adds the `pub mod setup_wcs_tilt;` line. No Cargo/build.rs/.github/scripts/.cargo/xtask path touched. Decision file present, provenance line present, module 68 lines.

**Results (merged with main 4ab3693e5e) - on the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43505259079**
- Quick gate: ok, app suites 194 s, 0 failed. Clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. Conclusion success. Not run locally (no `cfg(windows)` change).
- Which tests fail without which line: I verified by reading, and by the green run for the positive side, not by re-running mutations. `a_tilted_setup_wcs_refuses_generation_by_name` asserts the full named message, so it fails without the `collect_job` line; `a_wall_level_only_in_a_tilted_wcs_names_the_wcs` pins the selection.rs branch; `a_wcs_turned_only_about_z_still_generates` guards over-refusal. The author reports running the two deletions red/green; I did not repeat that.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. No test exercises a non-Mill setup (lathe/wire) under a tilted WCS, the NaN branch of `tilt_deg`, or a tilt just either side of 1e-9. The scope claim rests on the `Kind::Mill` guard being read, not pinned.
2. The headless doors (MCP/CLI) have no test of their own; they share `collect_job`, so this is by reading.
3. The quick gate ran the touched/mapped app suites only; the author lists rotated_wcs, rotary_verify, wcs_align, setup_align and others as run by hand, which I did not re-run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
